service.name: Singer and guitarist
service.serviceType: Acoustic singer and guitarist for cocktail hours, welcome drinks, patios, dinner parties and small weddings
service.description: One voice and a guitar, playing singer-songwriter, pop, soul and classic rock covers at a volume guests talk across, for cocktail hours, welcome drinks, patios, dinner parties, rehearsal dinners and small weddings across Denver, the Front Range and the Colorado mountain corridor, with sound included.

faqs.q: What does a singer and guitarist play?
faqs.a: Covers people know the words to: the singer-songwriter book, pop and soul from the last sixty years, and the acoustic end of classic rock. It's the one-musician version of the songs a cover band plays, sung at a level guests can talk across, and the set is built around the flow of your evening. The whole covers list is on the repertoire page.

faqs.q: Is one singer with a guitar enough for a cocktail hour?
faqs.a: For most cocktail hours and patios, yes. One voice and a guitar sound like live music from across a terrace and stay under the conversation, which is what the hour needs. Above about a hundred guests spread across a ballroom, the acoustic duo adds a second musician to fill the space.

faqs.q: Can a singer and guitarist play a wedding ceremony and the cocktail hour?
faqs.a: Yes, and that's a common booking: an instrumental prelude and processional, then the same musician sings the cocktail hour on the terrace. The musician's small sound system runs the officiant's microphone too, so the ceremony and the hour are one load-in and one contract.

faqs.q: How is this different from the solo guitarist page?
faqs.a: The voice. The solo guitarist page is instrumental guitar, jazz standards and Spanish-tinged sets that sit under a dinner without asking for attention. This page is a singer with a guitar, songs sung out front, for the hours where guests want to hear a voice and know the words.

faqs.q: Can we book a named singer instead of the format?
faqs.a: Yes. Tony Medina plays solo voice and acoustic guitar under his own name, blues and classic rock, and Tejas Singh fronts a duo that grows to a quartet. The format is the booking when you want the sound and don't need a name attached; the named acts are the booking when you want to hear exactly who's playing before you book.

Yes, and patios and lawns are its regular work. It needs a covered, level and dry spot with power run to it, and we agree a move-indoors plan with you ahead of time. Colorado evenings cool fast, and a guitar and a voice both slow down in the cold.
